codeReview.summary: Commit 4f742c7 broadens strategy detection and timeout messaging, but it does not satisfy the e2e-wasm-languages contract. The build path still executes host-installed toolchains instead of containerized builds, several component-language detections/build commands do not match the repo's WASM research, and the added tests stop at detection/parsing rather than representative multi-language builds or timeout enforcement.

issues.description: All of the new language builders ultimately run host binaries through exec.CommandContext via streamCommand/streamCommandWithEnv instead of a container runtime. That leaves success dependent on every runner having cargo-component, tinygo, clang+wasi-sdk, componentize-py, jco, and componentize-dotnet installed locally, so the feature's required containerized-build isolation was not implemented.

The new recognition heuristics are too broad for the component-model languages. hasDotnetProject accepts any .csproj/.fsproj, isPythonComponentizeProject accepts any requirements.txt/pyproject.toml + .py, and isJSComponentizeProject accepts any package.json + .js/.ts. Ordinary Node/Python/.NET repos will therefore be classified as supported instead of failing early with buildStrategy "unknown", which breaks the unsupported-language rejection behavior required by VAL-E2E-009.

Several of the new component builders do not follow the documented toolchains. Python and JS hardcode the world name "component" instead of the researched wasi:http/proxy world (and JS omits -w entirely when wit/ is absent), while the .NET path shells out to a standalone componentize-dotnet CLI even though the project research specifies dotnet build with BytecodeAlliance.ComponentizeSharp MSBuild integration. That makes multiple newly-advertised language paths unlikely to produce valid wasi-http components.

The added tests only exercise strategy detection helpers and parseBuildTimeout. There is no coverage for buildWasmArtifact, no representative repo builds for the new languages, and no test that a timed-out build job actually transitions to failed with the timeout snippet, so the highest-risk contract paths remain unverified.

Workers following backend-worker only read architecture/environment notes, so the stricter component-language requirements are easy to miss.

summary: Reviewed handoff 50ffca7a-1e84-46b9-9de0-0bd445f93828 and commit 4f742c7. The feature expands enums, heuristics, and timeout strings, but it does not deliver containerized multi-language WASM builds and uses overly broad detection plus mismatched component build commands for several of the newly claimed languages. Scrutiny status: fail.
